parole.significato: Speech, or a way of speaking, a narrative, logical discourse.
parole.testo: Unadapted borrowing from Middle French -logue, from Classical Latin -logus, from Ancient Greek -λόγος (-lógos, “a student of or specialist in a field; type of discourse”).

parole.significato: The quality of being imbecile; weakness; feebleness, especially of mind.
parole.testo: From Middle English inbecillite, from Middle French imbecilité, imbecillité, and its etymon Classical Latin imbēcillitās. By surface analysis, imbecile + -ity.

parole.significato: Unclean; ritually impure; unholy, desecrating a holy place or thing.
parole.testo: From Middle English prophane, from Middle French profane, prophaine, prophane and its etymon Classical Latin profānus (“not religious, unclean”) (also Late Latin prophānus), from pro- (“instead of”) + fānum (“temple”).

parole.significato: To violate (something sacred); to treat with abuse, irreverence, obloquy, or contempt; to desecrate
parole.testo: From Middle English prophanen, from Middle French profaner, prophaner and its etymon Classical Latin profānō (also Late Latin prophāno), from profānus + -ō (suffix forming verbs).

parole.significato: The right or chance to vote, express an opinion, or participate in a decision, especially in a democratic election.
parole.testo: From Middle English suffrage (“prayers or pleas on behalf of another”), from Middle French suffrage (from Old French suffrage) and its etymon Classical Latin suffrāgium (“support, vote, right of voting”).
